Messages.Author: David Zopf
Messages.Body:
Groups 2 and 3 are full.

Online VTES project at CCG Workshop has been activated.

New ranking system Coming in 2 weeks.

Next expansions to be set in pre-Gehenna timeline (1999-2003).

10th Anniversary set two different sets of 100 cards, each. 90 reprints of
staple Jyhad/VTES cards with new layout and card text, and 10 new cards,
each (200 cards total). Will be packaged in SteelRook cases oversized to
fit a VTES deck (110 cards).

Announced 'Build your own Storyline' a Prince's Choice of format and plot.
If a winner also wins a Continental Championship(?) plot line gets
incorporated into a future release.

Next storyline: "The Infernal Plague" a one-shot focusing on a Baali clan
corruption plotline. Brush up your infernal decks...

February Expansion: Kindred Most Wanted, includes Red List, and at its core
focuses on the Independent clans (DZ: presumably, lots of G4)

The "Double Edge" rumor from Lotus Noir was a playtested rule (dug out of 11
year old WotC playtest notes), which didn't make the expansion, but hasn't
been abandoned, either.

DaveZ
Atom Weaver

Basically, this rule has been spoiled in the french magazine Lotus Noir.

If you keep the edge one full turn, it transforms in a "Double Edge"
which gives the following advantages :

- you gain one pool at your untap if you have the Double Edge but it
comes from your prey pool
- it is worth 3 votes if you discard it during referendums

Somebody told that it was wet dreams from the writer of the article.
Seems that WotC and now WW developers must drink a lot at night ....

Regards

Mathieu

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
"Colin McGuigan" <magu...@BGONEspeakeasy.net> wrote in message
news:Rh6dnUTw1a_...@speakeasy.net...

years ago,
> > there was probably a reason. I'd guess the Gehenna playtesters
succeeded in
> > rediscovering that reason.

Now you've made me curious about what the original reason was! I would
think the reason it didn't end up in the original Jyhad rules would
likely have been in those same playtest notes, don't you think?

> [where "it" is the Double Edge]
>
> Probably because it makes wall decks even more fearsome in the 3-way
> than they are now?

That could make sense. I think it also might not be "worth" adding a
basic rule change to the rulebook this many years later, though,
considering that it is at least unusual (in my experience, anyhow) for
the Edge to be kept around the table in the first place.

At the same time, wall decks in the 3-way should be decent at holding
the Edge, but how well are they going to do at bleeding to get it in the
first place, if they're serious walls? And can they, practically
speaking, prevent their prey from getting the Edge sometimes too?
(Maybe more practically if it's an Anneke wall deck than otherwise, I
suppose, heh.)

I kind of wonder where Lotus Noir got that spoiler information - it
seems strange that White Wolf would have told them about the "Double
Edge" rule if they had decided not to implement it with the Gehenna
release. :-)

Josh

Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:


OK, I'll confess, I forgot that. Even so, it seems to me that if replacement
art would have solved the problem in the first place, Raven would never have
been born. The issue as I see it is that if you made the vampire look like
Stephanie Seymour, you'd still leave yourself open for problems. If you
didn't...well, then it wouldn't be Camille Devereux, either.

Granted, it was all kind of nebulous whether there was even a problem at
the time and, if so, how it could be solved. It may be that White Wolf
sees things differently than WotC did and will feel comfortable printing
something they'll call "Camille Devereux" (and a "Raven" as well). And
that would be just fine with me, mind you. I wasn't complaining. Just
pointing out that I wouldn't be totally surprised if it didn't happen.

Fred
